newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. Zaire envoy arrives for talks in Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Zaire envoy arrives for talks in Angola.

text.p: The U.N. special envoy on Zaire arrived in the Angolan capital Luanda on Wednesday for talks with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, officials said.
Mohamed Sahnoun, who also represents the Organisation of African Unity in his efforts to find peace in Zaire, was taken to the presidential palace.
The U.N. special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, told reporters Sahnoun would meet the president for talks on the relationship between Angola and Zaire.
Discussions would cover steps to ensure that Angola's rickety peace process, following two decades of civil war, would not suffer because of the fighting in neighbouring Zaire.
Rebels led by Laurent Kabila have taken control of over half of the vast African country.

Sahnoun was taken to the presidential palace on the outskirts of Luanda accompanied by Beye, who has been overseeing the two-year-old peace accord between the Angolan government and the former rebel movement UNITA.
Western diplomats in Luanda earlier said Angolan government soldiers were backing Kabila's forces.

Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko is a longtime ally of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi and his country was the site of many of its supply bases and logistics channels during the two decades it fought against the Angolan government.
UNITA also uses Zaire as its exit point for diamond sales mined in areas under its control in the northeast of Angola.
Regional analysts believe the Luanda government would like to cut off the former rebel group from its old supporters in the northern neighbour.
